title: India's Colombo Warm-Up Match Shortened by a Day Ahead of Sri Lanka Test Series
excerpt: The four-day practice fixture at the Nondescripts Cricket Club has been cut to three days as India prepare for a crucial WTC series starting August 15 in Galle.
body:
• India's warm-up match in Colombo ahead of the Sri Lanka Test series has been shortened from four days to three, according to Cricbuzz.
  • The team arrives in Colombo on August 4 and will play the practice match at the Nondescripts Cricket Club (NCC) Ground before traveling to Galle for the first Test on August 15.
  • The two-match series, part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle, is critical for both teams' qualification hopes.
  • India, led by captain Shubman Gill, are fifth in the WTC standings; Sri Lanka sit sixth.

India's planned four-day warm-up match in Colombo has been shortened by a day, Cricbuzz reported, as the team fine-tunes preparations for a high-stakes Test series against Sri Lanka that begins on August 15 in Galle.

The practice fixture at the Nondescripts Cricket Club Ground, originally scheduled from August 7 to 10, will now be a three-day affair. The NCC Ground sits close to the Sinhalese Sports Club, which will host the second Test from August 23 to 27, giving the visitors a chance to familiarize themselves with Colombo's conditions.

First Test Assignment in Sri Lanka Since 2017

This tour marks India's first Test visit to Sri Lanka in nearly a decade. Their last red-ball series on the island ended in a comprehensive 3-0 whitewash in 2017, when Virat Kohli's side dominated across all three formats during that tour.

The landscape has shifted considerably since then. India's squad, now captained by Shubman Gill, arrives after an innings victory over Afghanistan in a one-off Test earlier this year, though that match fell outside the current World Test Championship cycle. The team is expected to touch down in Colombo on August 4 to begin acclimatizing to the subcontinental heat and spin-friendly pitches.

WTC Stakes Are High

Both teams desperately need points in the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 standings. India currently occupy fifth place with four wins from nine matches, while Sri Lanka sit sixth with just one victory from four Tests. With the WTC final qualification race tightening, neither side can afford to drop points at home or away.

"This is India's first formal Test series visit to Sri Lanka since 2017 and carries immense weight for the ongoing WTC cycle."

— SportsTiger

Sri Lanka will be looking to bounce back after suffering a series defeat to the West Indies in their most recent Test assignment. The home side will hope spin-friendly conditions at Galle give them an edge, though India's recent record at the venue has been formidable.

Preparation Concerns

The shortening of the warm-up fixture raises questions about India's preparation time. Red-ball cricket demands specific conditioning and rhythm that cannot be replicated in net sessions alone. The practice match was intended to give batters time to adjust to Sri Lankan conditions and allow the bowling unit to find its lengths on unfamiliar surfaces.

India's most recent experience with shortened or inadequate warm-up time has been mixed. The team management has previously considered walking out of rain-affected practice matches, as happened ahead of a Test series in Australia, where coach Duncan Fletcher briefly contemplated abandoning a three-day warm-up after persistent rain.

The opening Test at the Galle International Cricket Stadium runs from August 15 to 19, followed by the second Test at the SSC Grounds in Colombo from August 23 to 27. Both matches are scheduled for a 10:00 AM IST start.

What to Watch

With senior players like Rohit Sharma having retired from Test cricket and the captaincy now in Gill's hands, the Sri Lanka series will be a defining assignment for India's new-look leadership. The warm-up, however shortened, will offer the first glimpse of India's likely combinations for the Galle Test, where spin has historically dominated proceedings.
